title: Concerns over AI investment returns rise as Nvidia's market cap ranking falls to third in the U.S.

content_html:
NVIDIA shares have continued to pull back, delivering huge paper gains to short sellers. According to S3 Partners data, NVIDIA's stock has fallen 35% since hitting a record high on October 6, and traders shorting the company's shares have reaped about $24 billion in paper profits in roughly 40 days.

On Monday local time, NVIDIA shares fell another 4.1%, after the stock last week posted its largest weekly decline since April 2025, when Trump announced tariff hikes. As a result, NVIDIA ended the day as the third-largest U.S. company by market capitalization, behind Apple and Microsoft, the first time it has fallen to that position since May 2025.

Behind the market swings, investors are worried about the sustainability of capital-intensive AI infrastructure buildout. The U.S. tech sector had already been volatile for several weeks, and in the U.S. midterm elections, several candidates who advocated limiting unchecked data center expansion won, further deepening market concerns about returns on AI industry investment and energy and infrastructure costs.

S3 data shows that as the NVIDIA selloff accelerated in early November, short selling increased in tandem. Currently, short interest accounts for about 1.22% of the float, equivalent to about $46 billion in notional value.

The pullback in NVIDIA's stock reflects a reassessment of AI capital spending, industry valuations, and growth expectations, and the investment logic of the AI supply chain is facing a new round of scrutiny.
